hook: Fake 'digital arrest' takes *₹33.4 lakh* from a Masab Tank retiree
hook_b: Fake 'digital arrest' takes *₹33.4 lakh* from a Masab Tank retiree
tldr: Fraudsters posing as Karnataka police and an IPS officer told a retired LIC employee her Aadhaar was linked to a ₹3 crore laundering case and kept her under 'digital arrest'.

beats.what: Between Aug 31 and Sept 22 she made four RTGS transfers for 'verification of funds', 'security deposit' and 'e-court charges'.
beats.why: The callers claimed 247 debit cards, one in her name, were seized from a criminal, and said an FIR and arrest warrant existed.
beats.care: Police never place anyone under 'digital arrest' over a call; the script told her not to tell family or bank staff.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: She broke a recurring deposit early and pledged gold to pay; the complaint was filed with Hyderabad cybercrime police on Monday.

cards.q: Should banks pause large transfers by senior citizens for a cooling-off check?

qs: What should a bank do when a customer's explanation sounds scripted?
How can families spot that an elder is under a 'digital arrest'?

facts.t: Fraudsters claimed *247 debit cards*, one in her name, were seized from a criminal.

steps.e: Fake IPS officer claims ₹3 crore laundering case
Numbers go dead; she realises the fraud

viz.verdict: Three weeks of calls, four transfers, months before the fraud was spotted

learn.t: Digital arrest = a scam where callers posing as officials keep a victim on video/phone 'under arrest' and demand money; no such arrest exists in law

watch: Whether cybercrime police trace the accounts.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Retired LIC employee loses ₹33.4 lakh in digital arrest scam in Hyderabad

fact: A 65-year-old Masab Tank retiree lost *₹33.4 lakh* in a fake 'digital arrest'
twist: A bank official did question one big transfer, but she gave the cover story the fraudsters had told her to use.
